data.claim: contended inverts waiting.wait_for_graph, which recomputes a waiter's edges from its STALE recorded ask (lease.waiting globs); a waiter that narrowed its globs after the refused widening is still named for the holder whose file it gave up.
data.falsifier: test_a_waiter_that_narrowed_away_is_not_held_contended asserts 'T2' not in contended(...)[T1] after T2 narrows src/b.py,src/a.py back to src/b.py -- it FAILED before the fix (contended=={'T1':['T2']}) and PASSES after.
data.mechanism: update --globs wider is refused and records lease.waiting with the refused globs; update --globs narrower succeeds (retarget keeps the same lease.event) so the recorded ask stays stale; wait_for_graph recomputes from the stale ask; contended inverts to holder->waiters; the heartbeat surfaces it as a false YIELD REQUESTED.
data.probe: Write the regression test, run it on the unfixed code, then after the fix.
data.probe_output: FAILED tests/test_lease_yield_disjoint_waiter.py (contended=={'T1':['T2']}), then after filtering contended by current-glob overlap: 1 passed.
data.question: Does leasebreak.contended name a waiter whose current globs no longer overlap the holder?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED (R34560c7a23): test_a_waiter_that_narrowed_away_is_not_held_contended FAILED on unfixed code (contended=={'T1':['T2']}) then PASSED after filtering contended by current-glob overlap; uv run pytest tests/test_lease_yield_disjoint_waiter.py -> 1 failed before, 1 passed after.

Researched the claim before editing (ddflow recall yield_requested disjoint globs), read the code path heartbeat._yield_request -> leasebreak.contended -> waiting.wait_for_graph, and recorded the bug before fixing.

Filtered leasebreak.contended to drop a waiter when none of its CURRENT globs (it.globs) overlaps the holder's live lease, via conflicts(wanted, holder_lease.globs, shared_globs). Regression test added and passing; cycle-detection and yield-surface tests unaffected.

chunk_findings.detail: The filter that drops stale yield edges only runs when `wanted` is non-empty. When the waiter’s current `globs` is empty (`wit.globs == []`, or `wit` is absent so `wanted == []`), the condition `wanted and not conflicts(...)` is false, so the stale edge is still appended. That state has no current waiter glob overlapping the holder’s lease, exactly the false `YIELD REQUESTED` this change is meant to remove. Concrete repro: T1 holds `src/a.py`; T2 has an old recorded wait for T1 and then is narrowed to no file globs. `LB.contended(st, cfg, now).get("T1", [])` still contains `"T2"` even though T2 no longer has any glob that overlaps `src/a.py`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leasebreak.py:contended

chunk_findings.detail: `contended` checks `if it is not None and it.lease is not None and wanted and not conflicts(wanted, it.lease.globs, shared): continue`, but `it` is the *holder* (item_id), not the waiter. Therefore, `it.lease.globs` are the holder's lease globs, not the waiter's. The function intends to check whether the *waiter's* current globs conflict with the *holder's* lease globs, but comparing `wanted` (the waiter's globs) against `it.lease.globs` (the *holder's* lease globs) via `not conflicts(...)` means it checks if the *waiter's* globs overlap the *holder's* globs (which is what we want), but `it` is retrieved via `st.items.get(item_id)` where `item_id` is the held item. If the holder item's lease globs are accessed, it compares the waiter's globs against the holder's lease globs; however, if the holder's lease is `None` (e.g., if the item is in a state where `lease` is None or abandoned), `it.lease` raises an `AttributeError` crashing `contended` on any heartbeat. Furthermore, if `it.lease` is checked, `it` is the holder, so `it.lease.globs` is the holder's own lease globs compared to the waiter's globs. Wait, if `wanted` does not conflict with `it.lease.globs`, it skips. But if the holder's lease is `None`, `it.lease` is `None`, so `it.lease.globs` throws an AttributeError.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leasebreak.py:144

chunk_findings.detail: The new filter does not implement the contract it states. The drop runs only when `wanted` is truthy (`it is not None and it.lease is not None and wanted and not conflicts(...)`). A waiter that has given up every file has `globs == []` (or is missing from `st.items`, so `wanted` is forced to `[]`); that short-circuit skips `conflicts` and still `append`s the waiter. Given T1 leased on `src/a.py` and a wait-for edge from T2 whose current globs are `[]`, `contended` still returns `{"T1": ["T2"]}`, so heartbeat keeps printing YIELD REQUESTED for a waiter that holds no overlapping glob — the same false yield B38ebc3e392 describes, at the empty end of “narrowed away”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leasebreak.py:contended

chunk_findings.detail: The regression only asserts the negative (`"T2" not in contended(...)["T1"]`) after a narrow to a disjoint glob. It never asserts the complementary case the function still promises: a waiter whose current globs still overlap the holder’s lease must remain in `contended`. `assert "T2" in WG.standing(...)` does not lock that, because standing is not `leasebreak.contended`. An over-filter that always returns `{}` (or that treats every `conflicts` result as “drop”) passes this test while suppressing a real YIELD REQUESTED.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_yield_disjoint_waiter.py:test_a_waiter_that_narrowed_away_is_not_held_contended

chunk_findings.detail: `contended` checks `if it is not None and it.lease is not None and wanted and not conflicts(wanted, it.lease.globs, shared): continue`, but `it` is the *holder* (item_id), not the waiter. Therefore, `it.lease.globs` are the holder's lease globs, not the waiter's. The function intends to check whether the *waiter's* current globs conflict with the *holder's* lease globs, but comparing `wanted` (the waiter's globs) against `it.lease.globs` (the *holder's* lease globs) via `not conflicts(...)` means it checks if the *waiter's* globs overlap the *holder's* globs (which is what we want), but `it` is retrieved via `st.items.get(item_id)` where `item_id` is the held item. If the holder item's lease globs are accessed, it compares the waiter's globs against the holder's lease globs; however, if the holder's lease is `None` (e.g., if the item is in a state where `lease` is None or abandoned), `it.lease` raises an `AttributeError` crashing `contended` on any heartbeat. Furthermore, if `it.lease` is checked, `it` is the holder, so `it.lease.globs` is the holder's own lease globs compared to the waiter's globs. Wait, if `wanted` does not conflict with `it.lease.globs`, it skips. But if the holder's lease is `None`, `it.lease` is `None`, so `it.lease.globs` throws an AttributeError.

chunk_findings.detail: The new filter does not implement the contract it states. The drop runs only when `wanted` is truthy (`it is not None and it.lease is not None and wanted and not conflicts(...)`). A waiter that has given up every file has `globs == []` (or is missing from `st.items`, so `wanted` is forced to `[]`); that short-circuit skips `conflicts` and still `append`s the waiter. Given T1 leased on `src/a.py` and a wait-for edge from T2 whose current globs are `[]`, `contended` still returns `{"T1": ["T2"]}`, so heartbeat keeps printing YIELD REQUESTED for a waiter that holds no overlapping glob — the same false yield B38ebc3e392 describes, at the empty end of “narrowed away”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leasebreak.py:contended

chunk_findings.detail: The regression only asserts the negative (`"T2" not in contended(...)["T1"]`) after a narrow to a disjoint glob. It never asserts the complementary case the function still promises: a waiter whose current globs still overlap the holder’s lease must remain in `contended`. `assert "T2" in WG.standing(...)` does not lock that, because standing is not `leasebreak.contended`. An over-filter that always returns `{}` (or that treats every `conflicts` result as “drop”) passes this test while suppressing a real YIELD REQUESTED.
